# Output identity repair and merge proof

PR 137 at 1fbe46c closes the original F001/F002/N001 review. The output table and conflict target both use project plus governance-relative path. The regression inserts an identical path into a second project and reads both records back, so a project-filter-only happy path cannot hide a namespace collision.

Notice IDs derive from the output project and writer commit, never a clock reading. The HTTP regression checks both IDs and two held FYIs, not only distinct files. A committed identity remains useful even when notification continuations complete out of order.

For diagnostics, distinguish real absence from failed lookup. The guard returns an HTTP response whose meta carries adapter causes; decoding that cause preserves the error without sending after a refused audit. This was source-verified, not newly fault-injected.

Merge verification used main-parent equality for main-owned role-request code and direct checks of shared endpoint/schema wiring. The last merge imported main routing-table code; it was not literally a documentation-only delta, but the s06 files were unchanged. Generic shim tests iterate the native manifest, so adding output/outputs makes them participate automatically.

Exact-head CI ran 2,021 tests successfully, including six output HTTP cases, the store boundary and shim controls. No local build or probe. Security's answer-authority verdict and performance remain separate.

magicWand fulfilled: committed regressions now test the owning namespace and actual notification effect. Preserve those boundaries when later changing output storage or delivery.
